name: Magbish
overview: Magbish is a male figure mentioned in the book of Ezra whose descendants played a role in the post-exilic restoration of Judah. His sons returned to Judah after the Babylonian captivity, marking him as part of the community that sought to rebuild and reestablish themselves in the land. Beyond this, specific tribal affiliation or additional personal details are not recorded in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Magbish appears as a proper name in the biblical record, with a possible meaning of 'thick.' There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, and no further titles or alternate names are associated with him in the Scripture.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture indicates that Magbish is a descendant of Jacob, situating him within the broader covenantal lineage of Israel. His sons are noted for their return to Judah after the exile, but no other family relationships are detailed beyond this.
scriptureSignificance: Magbish's significance lies in his connection to the returning exiles who came back to Judah to restore the community and worship after captivity. His mention underscores the faithfulness of God's people in maintaining their identity through generations and their commitment to return to their homeland. As a descendant of Jacob, Magbish represents the continuity of God's promises through the line of Israel despite the trials of exile.
